target_customer: Donors funding medical care for low income patients; operates as a nonprofit
problem: People in poor countries cannot afford surgeries, and donors lacked a direct, transparent way to fund a specific patient's care.
business_model: nonprofit crowdfunding with donations passed 100 percent to care; operating costs from philanthropic grants

founders.name: Chase Adam
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page he later co-founded Grove; coverage says Watsi took 18 months to launch on about $3,000 (search snippet).

competitors.name: Kiva
competitors.what: Microlending platform that coverage compared Watsi to as 'Kiva for healthcare'

technical_complexity.rationale: A donation site with patient profiles; the hard parts were partner clinics and payment logistics.

defensibility.rationale: Trust, transparency and clinic partnerships mattered more than software.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed it; it stayed an independent nonprofit.

market_need_then: Medical expenses in developing countries and a rise of crowdfunding sites in 2012 made a direct patient funding model timely.

branding.name_origin: Named after a town the founder was traveling through, per a search summary of Watsi's blog and Wikipedia; not verified from the primary page.
branding.domain_note: Uses watsi.org; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Originally a blue cross with a white triangle; changed in 2014 to white triangles on a blue circle after a legal threat from a health insurer

branding.brand_signature: Patient profile cards with photo and story

rebrands.to: white triangles on a blue circle
rebrands.why: Legal threat from a multi-billion dollar health insurance company, per TechCrunch (2014-02-26).

branding.community_and_virality: Held a logo bonfire event to mark the change, per a Watsi blog snippet; strong press coverage as YC's first nonprofit.

brand_strength.rationale: Widely covered as the first YC nonprofit with a recognizable donor community.

outcome_analysis: Watsi launched in August 2012, became YC's first nonprofit in the W13 batch and raised a $1.2M philanthropic seed in July 2013 from donors including Paul Graham and Tencent. It later raised a $3.5M philanthropic growth round and claims to have funded care for tens of thousands of patients, relying on a trusted brand and transparency.
notes: A later $3.5M philanthropic growth round (VentureBeat, led by Paul Graham, Tencent, Pershing Square Foundation, Ron Conway, Vinod Khosla) has no date in the snippet seen so it is not recorded as a round. YC page says founded 2011; CB Insights says 2012. The watsi.org about page returned 403 and was not worked around. Watsi is a nonprofit so rounds are philanthropic gifts. Jesse Cooke appears as co-founder only on a Wikipedia mirror not opened, so omitted. Competitor GiveForward appears only on a CB Insights directory comparison, undated, so omitted.
